features.name: op_first_person_singular_pronoun_count
features.definition: How many explicit first-person singular pronouns appear in the original argument text?
features.spec: Input: df['argument'] (OP argument body only; title excluded). If missing/non-string return null. Count case-insensitive whole-word regex matches of r"\b(I|me|my|mine|myself|I'm|I've|I'll|I'd)\b" (treat curly apostrophes as straight; contractions with I counted once each, not also as 'I'). Return integer count; empty string gives 0. Raw mechanical count over current text, including any quoted text and edits.

features.name: has_op_first_person_singular_pronoun
features.definition: Does the original argument contain at least one explicit first-person singular pronoun?
features.spec: Return 1 if df['op_first_person_singular_pronoun_count'] > 0, 0 if it equals 0, null if it is null.

h0: has_op_first_person_singular_pronoun has no association with the probability of view change.
h1: Discussions with has_op_first_person_singular_pronoun = 1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
note: Presence is the primary measurement; the count is a supporting feature. Pronoun list is an operational assumption (I, me, my, mine, myself and I-contractions). Raw regex counts include quoted text and edits, and the current argument text may contain post-outcome edits or delta announcements; these are not filtered. Pronouns are nearly universal in OP arguments, so variation may be small. Association only, not causal.
